title: 2026-11-05_Hajime_Botnet_Investigation_394
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux IoT device infected with the Hajime botnet. Your goal is to identify and contain the malicious activity while preserving evidence for further analysis.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Hajime botnet is a peer-to-peer (P2P) botnet that targets Linux IoT devices. It spreads by exploiting default or weak credentials and then establishes a P2P network for communication and command and control (C2). The botnet is known for its persistence mechanisms and ability to maintain a presence on infected devices. This training will guide you through identifying and containing the malicious activity. No submission is required for this introductory level.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the compromised host `bot1` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. You can also access the C2 server `c2-server` with the same credentials. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the compromised host `bot1` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. You can also access the C2 server `c2-server` with the same credentials. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Identify the C2 Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server. Submit the service name as the answer.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the compromised host `bot1` using SSH with the provided credentials.
2. List all services, including inactive ones, using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`.
3. Look for unfamiliar service names or misspellings of legitimate services.
4. Identify the service responsible for sending beacon to the C2 server.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual descriptions or startup behavior.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name is the hidden flag.

levels.title: Determine the C2 Communication Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication. Submit the port number as the answer.
levels.solution:
1. From the previous task, you have identified the service responsible for sending beacon to the C2 server.
2. Inspect the service configuration using the command `systemctl cat <service>`.
3. Pay particular attention to the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
4. Check the script to find the communication port with the C2 server.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The communication port is the hidden flag.

levels.title: Identify the C2 Beacon Scheduler
levels.content: Investigators suspect how the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity. Submit the timer name as the answer.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers using the command `systemctl list-timers --all`.
2. Look for timers associated with the service identified in the previous tasks.
3. Inspect the timer configuration using the command `systemctl cat <timer>`.
4. Identify the timer responsible for scheduling the C2 beacon service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers associated with the service identified in the previous tasks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer name is the hidden flag.
